title: Graceful schema evolution + partial-apply protocol for function-call params
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a compact JSON-schema evolution and partial-apply protocol that lets the runtime accept parameter sets that are a strict superset or subset of a function's canonical schema. Goals: 1) enable safe rollout of added or deprecated fields without breaking older SDKs; 2) allow short-lived 'partial apply' usage where callers intentionally omit optional blocks and server-side defaults or cached prefixes are used; 3) produce deterministic, machine-readable diagnostic envelopes for consumers and SDKs (for human UX, telemetry, and automatic remediation). This ticket covers schema-format additions, runtime validation behavior, error code taxonomy, and an initial compatibility shim for older SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts param payloads that omit non-required blocks and returns a "partial_apply" result with applied defaults and canonicalized shape
Deprecated field aliases are resolved automatically when requested via header X-Param-Compat=alias:v1 and emit a PC_DEPRECATED_ALIASED warning in diagnostics

A stable, minimal diagnostics envelope is returned for validation failures with machine codes (PC_MISSING_REQUIRED, PC_TYPE_MISMATCH, PC_COERCE_WARN, PC_EXTRA_FIELD, PC_PARTIAL_APPLY, PC_STREAM_ABORT)
SDKs can opt into strict or permissive validation mode via request param or header; permissive mode receives coercion hints and non-fatal warnings
Design document and sample schemas published in the FunctionCallReliability Confluence page and an initial runtime flag gated behind runtime-2.1 feature flag
Integration tests demonstrating streaming tool calls where parameter validation errors can be emitted mid-stream and cause a graceful stream abort with PC_STREAM_ABORT
technical_notes: Introduce a compact param-profile section in function manifest: 'compat': { 'min_version': 1, 'aliases': { 'oldName': 'newName' }, 'partial_apply': true }
Partial-apply semantics: server merges incoming params with default-provider (cache, defaults, or model-generated) and emits a canonicalized_params object in the response diagnostics
Validation pipeline stages: parse -> alias resolution -> coercion (type/format) -> required check -> post-merge validation -> telemetry tagging
Telemetry: emit validation.code and validation.path tags, and a compact validation.summary string to minimize cardinality while keeping debuggability
Deprecation mapping: use alias table only when header X-Param-Compat enables it; otherwise alias usage is PC_EXTRA_FIELD
Backward compatibility: SDKs that do not send X-Param-Compat receive stricter errors; we provide an opt-in header for gradual rollouts

Streaming interactions: validation messages may be sent as 'diagnostic' events with a stable envelope; fatal errors trigger a stream abort token with code PC_STREAM_ABORT and graceful teardown message
migration_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): Add 'compat' block to manifest parsing. Enable alias resolution only when X-Param-Compat header is present.
Phase 2 (beta): Enable partial-apply behind runtime-2.1 flag. Add permissive SDK test harness and example code. Publish Confluence design.
Phase 3 (rollout): Flip default for non-enterprise tenants after 2-week beta, while keeping ability to opt-out via header. Monitor telemetry for PC_PARTIAL_APPLY and PC_COERCE_WARN rates.
Phase 4 (deprecations): After stable rollout, publish deprecation timeline for old field names and provide CLI migration tool to rewrite manifests in repos
test_plan: Unit tests for alias resolution, coercion rules, and canonicalization logic
Integration tests: permissive and strict SDKs hitting the same function manifest; confirm expected diagnostics and HTTP status codes
Stream tests: simulate long-running tool that emits validation warnings mid-stream and a final PC_STREAM_ABORT on fatal schema mismatch
Chaos test: inject malformed alias tables and confirm runtime falls back to strict rejection with PC_EXTRA_FIELD
Performance test: measure median and p95 validation overhead (target <2ms median added per request for common manifests)
